name: Catalan Romanesque Churches of the Vall de Boí
description: Tucked into a narrow valley in the high Pyrenees of Catalonia, the Vall de Boí holds nine stone churches built in the 11th and 12th centuries. Their slender Lombard-style bell towers rise above villages ringed by small walled fields and steep mountain pastures. The interiors were once covered in rich wall paintings, and many originals now hang in Barcelona's MNAC, replaced on site by copies.
